A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-EDL research despite the changed title and formatting. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, OOD detection, adversarial detection, ablation, and inference-time results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds broader baseline comparisons, few-shot evaluation, uncertainty visualizations, and runtime studies.

M1.justification: The transformation-based evidence generation, intra/inter-class conflict calculation, aggregation, and exponential evidence adjustment are unchanged. New explanations and evaluations with additional backbones do not introduce a different C-EDL procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on Tiny-ImageNet object images paired with CUB fine-grained bird images, extending the represented ID/OOD distributions beyond the original nine datasets. Table 5 evaluates this pairing under few-shot conditions. Oxford Flowers is newly labeled low-shot, but its documented data preparation and existing results remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The original comparator set remains. v2 Table 4 adds a standard deterministic network, standalone MC-Dropout, ABNN, an EDL-head fine-tuning baseline, and EMM. Table 6 additionally evaluates RED, distinct from the retained R-EDL baseline. These substantially broaden the comparisons beyond the original EDL-focused evaluation.

E3.justification: New protocols include 5-way 1-shot and 5-shot evaluation with a pretrained ResNet50-Wide backbone, numerical AUROC, and L2PGD maximum perturbation 0.1 in Table 5. Table 13 adds timing evaluation across LeNet and SeNet, datasets, and transformation counts. Existing benchmark settings remain documented as before; the new pretraining specification conflicts with Appendix C.5's retained blanket no-pretraining statement.

E4.justification: v2 adds score-distribution diagnostics for ID, OOD, and adversarial inputs, a CIFAR-10 three-class simplex analysis, comparative runtime-versus-coverage analysis, and runtime scaling across model sizes and transformation counts. These examine additional aspects of uncertainty behavior and computational practicality. Existing attack, threshold, dropout, and augmentation ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten independent runs, random seeds, and results using the same ± reporting format. Additional result entries do not introduce a stated change in repetitions, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: All eight original result tables retain their numerical entries after matching v2 Tables 1–3 and 7–11. New outcomes include broader-baseline and RED comparisons, few-shot results, and additional timings. For example, new Table 5 reports 1-shot AUROC of 69.76% ± 5.00 for C-EDL versus 64.50% ± 4.27 for EDL. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements between versions under an existing setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 1, and Appendix A derivations are substantively unchanged. Equation renumbering and moving the evidence-set definition inline are presentation changes. Added discussion of numerical stability and conflict-formula motivation does not revise the mathematics or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same post-hoc robustness claims, theoretical contribution, and approximately 55% OOD and 90% adversarial coverage reductions. The rewritten conclusion preserves the original scope and efficiency claims; new experiments mainly supply additional supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking cross-view disagreement primarily to epistemic instability, explains the intended handling of low-evidence inter-class conflict, and interprets the new simplex visualization. It also discusses few-shot applicability, RED comparisons, and choosing transformation counts according to deployment-time constraints. Most existing interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds Tiny-ImageNet/CUB dataset descriptions, identifies the new pretrained backbone, and reports additional inference times and model parameter counts. Existing code access, hardware, training hyperparameters, and augmentation settings remain unchanged. Implementation details for the new comparisons and few-shot protocol remain limited.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new datasets and comparators, plus several contextual UQ citations. Section 4.2 explicitly distinguishes C-EDL's single-model, post-hoc transformed views from ECML's separately trained input views. The broader related-work organization and central research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, affiliations are updated, acknowledgments are added, and selected captions, evaluation passages, and the conclusion are rewritten. Method explanations are expanded locally. The overall section structure and most existing prose are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables, score-density plots captioned as AUROC plots, and a simplex visualization. The original main-text coverage boxplot moves into the appendix, other boxplot panels are regrouped, and dataset examples expand. Comparative tables gain grouped headers, alongside document-wide typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator tests, challenging few-shot evaluation, and computational scaling studies strengthen the empirical support beyond v1's mainly LeNet-based evaluation. The gain is limited by incomplete documentation and new inconsistencies: Table 5 specifies pretraining while Appendix C.5 denies it, and Appendix B.4's per-input timings and S-EDL sample count do not reconcile with the accompanying documentation. The added evidence is useful, but its presentation and reproducibility need refinement.
